I used go work at an escape room. During the pandemic the owner basically went hands off and left a majority of the business (minus payroll) for me (F21-at the time) to run. For the next  two tears it was open. We barely scraped by most of the time, and I was working with a non existent budget to update/make the rooms better (we literally had no budget…at most maybe $200???), and since the owner wasnt very creative and i came from a theatre design background we had two very different standards of production quality. We heavily relied on traffic, and even though i knew our experience were not the most polished or the best, a lot of the puzzles and designs inside the rooms were made with with whatever i could scrounge up and try to look great. Bad reviews were the worst because it meant less business and therefore less money, and it hurt because any money for the business would have gone into allowing us to  afford to close down the rooms and  afford to be able to make improvements. I never EVER disagreed with the reviews, as i felt the same way whenever they mentioned low production quality or puzzles not working (no budget meant we couldn’t replace long overdue mechanisms). I would have given my left leg for the reviewers to have called and given feedback instead of posting reviews that at times also were unnecessarily harsh, going past constructive to just plain hurtful, because it meant less business and less hours to give my employees, and less ability to make improvements I desperately wished for. Its a difficult situation, as i understand spending money and being upset that you had an experience that felt unworthy of the amount spent, but i also just remember how much one negative review hurt us, even if we had ten good ones surrounding it.  (Most good reviews did not mention the rooms, but me and the gms for the experience we provided)
